review.comment: You use Number(), trim, and toFixed(2) well; the four README examples behave correctly. The check !people > 0 is parsed as (!people) > 0, so negative totals or counts still print a share. people is never validated as a positive integer. Next: use Number.isFinite on total and people before dividing, then require total > 0 and Number.isInteger(people) && people >= 1.

You fixed Number.isFinite on total and people, and people=0 now errors; all four README examples pass. total=0 still prints a share because you check total < 0 instead of total > 0, and non-integer people (e.g. 3.5) are accepted. Next: require total > 0 and Number.isInteger(people) && people >= 1 before dividing.

You fixed integer validation for people; Number(), trim, and toFixed(2) handle all four README examples correctly. total=0 still prints a share because the check uses total < 0 instead of total > 0. Next: require total > 0 before dividing.

You fixed total validation with total <= 0 and kept Number.isInteger(people) >= 1 from your prior submission. Parsing uses Number() with trim, Number.isFinite guards, and toFixed(2) for display. All README acceptance cases pass.
